description: Climate Ready Infrastructure and Sensitive Sites Protocol (CRISSP) is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative; NOAA Climate Program Office, Climate Adaptation Partnerships Program; Great Lakes Integrated Sciences + Assessments (GLISA - A NOAA CAP/RISA Program). Great Lakes cities are at different stages of preparedness for extreme weather associated with climate change. This site guides municipalities through a easy-to-implement process to develop a vulnerability assessment. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – General, High Winds, Severe Winter Weather. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Water Infrastructure – General, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater, Water Infrastructure – Wastewater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
